questions.prompt_markup: Prove that sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 for every angle θ, using the unit circle.
questions.correct_answer: The point at θ is (cos θ, sin θ) and lies on x² + y² = 1, so cos²θ + sin²θ = 1.

questions.prompt: A right triangle has legs a and b, hypotenuse c, and acute angle θ opposite a. Prove sin²θ + cos²θ = 1.

questions.prompt: θ is in quadrant II. Prove sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 using a reference triangle, explaining what happens to the signs.
questions.prompt_markup: θ is in quadrant II. Prove sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 using a reference triangle, explaining what happens to the signs.
questions.correct_answer: The point is (x, y) with x < 0 < y; the reference triangle has legs |x|, |y| and hypotenuse 1, so |x|² + |y|² = 1, and squares remove the signs: cos²θ + sin²θ = 1.
